system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.

solution.what: Penn IIIF manifests of Codex 531, 533-537 saved; Codex 533 and 531 images fetched; every leaf of Codex 533 paged: about 35 bare cipher runs, no decipherment.

Tried the interlined Codex 531 cipher (System A, dotted 1-3 digit groups; upstream research/medici_bia names it a key-rebuild source) against Codex 533: a different system (Codex 533 uses run-on two-sign groups with an eleventh sign).
Homophonic annealers with an Italian 4-gram model tested on a synthetic text of 1,500 letters: best -4.59 per letter against -4.10 for the truth, so a keyless solve was judged unreliable.
Found System B letters in Codex 534 with the recipient's interlinear decipherment (f. 14r, 30 Oct 1690); built key v1 (20 groups) from f. 14r and froze it (sha256 8bedce85...).
Held-out test of key v1 on four interlined segments of f. 15r (39 groups): 39 of 39; 200 shuffled keys at most 28.2%. Caveat: the reader knew the key when reading the interline.
Key v2 (22 groups) from ff. 14r and 15r, frozen (sha256 64783ab8...) before the clean test.

Clean held-out test on f. 21r (5 Dec 1690): cipher transcribed from crops with the interline blanked and frozen before the interline was read; 76 of 92 covered groups match (82.6%); 200 shuffled keys at most 35.9% (mean 23.9%).

Codex 533 transcribed twice: pass A forward (agent knew the key), pass B backward by a blind agent; 704 of pass B's 811 signs agreed (pass A has 850); all 116 disagreement sites checked on full-size crops (112 settled, 4 left open); two reconciled transcriptions frozen.

Cosimo's c-with-loop is the clerks' w; w6 = i (one interline on 534 f. 396v plus 38 contexts) and 91 = u (f. 21r) added as key v3 (frozen, sha256 bdc8b174...); ww = o and 62 = q kept apart as context-only values (sha256 f5115d38...).

35 runs of Codex 533 decoded with key v3 and the context values: 318 of the 401 groups in the decode (79.3%) take a letter; 15 runs read whole, 15 in part, 5 not read; the word share is in fraction_read.
Bare System B passages of Codex 534 ff. 114r-116v and Codex 531 f. 4r (1694) decoded with key v2 and read at about 85-95% (estimate); code numbers open.

A second AI agent transcribed and read Codex 533 ff. 1r-1v blind from the images and froze its reading before opening the first agent's notes: same cipher words, digits confirmed, clear-text corrections ('reputatione', 'che', 'ci fanno vergogna', the instructions on 1v). It had seen a key file note naming some words.

Searched for editions or studies of the letters and the cipher, and for any 1690s report that the Electress wished to return or separate: none found in the sources opened; Acton not read; Florence State Archive and Medici Archive Project unreachable.

Recount by words after Daniel Bourdeau's review of PR #665 (readings/words_533_strict.tsv): of 87 cipher words in Cosimo's 35 runs, 30 sure, 42 with the context-only values; L01 9 of 16 and L70 0 of 1 sure, both now read in part.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 825 tokens, 40 types, it-modern order 4: reading -2.592 per letter; random keys -6.86 (z 6.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.371 (mean -3.482, z 14.0); annealer on the real text -2.832. Verdict: pass.

Integration check of pull request #665 (15 and 16 Nov 2026). scripts/run_tests.py re-run: the eight recorded hashes match; key v1 on f. 15r 39 of 39 (shuffles at most 28.2%); key v2 on the held-out f. 21r 76 of 92 = 82.6% (200 shuffled keys at most 35.9%, mean 23.9%); as recorded. Images: Penn's Colenda manifest of Ms. Codex 533 answers and gives the rights statement NoC-US; crops of f. 1r (runs a-f, 69 groups) and f. 22r (run a, 28 groups) fetched from Penn's IIIF server and compared sign by sign with transcriptions/reconciled_533_v2.tsv: all 97 groups agree at 1900 px, one 6/0 place in 1r run c not safe at that size. A decoder written here from key_v3.json and the context values reproduces the letters of readings/runs_533.tsv for those runs and of the four bare passages (P1 273 of 296 groups on the key, P2 139 of 149, P3 50 of 55, P4 16 of 17). Word count: readings/words_533_strict.tsv recounted, 30 sure of 87 and 42 with the context-only values; the review of 15 Nov had counted 37 and 51 by admitting seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which README Conventions counts as holes, so the contributor's lower figures stand. Reading reviews by the reviewer: L01, L21, L35 and P1 B; P2, P3, P4 A; L25, L26, L28, L56, L63 and L70 marked decoded, not read (isolated words, the clear sentence around them not transcribed). Credit role set to new cipher with solution. No earlier target, catalogue entry or lead uses this key. Not checked: Codex 534 (the interlines that give the key, and the held-out f. 21r) and the bare passages on the images, the other Codex 533 runs on the image. No person has checked any of it.

Decrypt audit (research/decrypt_audit): the script compared P1 and P2 only and found 51 of 113 words of bare/P1_it.txt and P2_it.txt departing from key/key_entries.tsv applied to the group files. All 17 texts checked with an own read-only snippet: of 892 groups 781 take the key's letter as printed in the decode files, 77 have no value, 27 letters of Codex 533 rest on re-read digits marked * in the decode files (not key values), and two places do not follow (L19 group 55 printed ?, L35 'della' with five letters for four groups). The departing words of P1 and P2 are mostly the clerk's clear text. In the reading files: 12 clear words printed in capitals as cipher (P1, P2, P4), 17 words with a consonant doubled without a bracket, 14 places with a letter changed, dropped or supplied without a bracket, and 23 words of Codex 533 whose re-read digit is marked in the decode file but not in the reading. No key value was missing; no file but NOTES.md and this profile changed. No image compared.

Decrypt audit, marking, no letter changed: 9 places bracketed in bare/P1_it.txt, P2_it.txt, readings/L01_it.txt and L35_it.txt; 27 re-read-digit stars carried from the decode files into 23 words of eight readings/L*_it.txt files; 12 clear words re-cased from capitals in P1, P2 and P4; 5 places where a decoded letter or code group is not printed are stated in header lines instead; a header line added to 13 files stating the marks and what 'normalized' covers. The generating scripts were not changed, so a re-run would remove the marks.

Clear Italian around the cipher runs of ff. 25r, 26r, 28v, 56r-57r, 63r and 70v transcribed sentence by sentence (readings/clear_context_533.md and .tsv), after the review of pull request #665 listed these six entries as decoded, not read. Pass B by a separate AI agent from image crops only, blind to every transcription and to the decoded words (readings/verify/clear_passB_blind_2026-11-16.md); pass A by the packaging agent, made after pass B and knowing the decoded words (agreement an upper bound). Clear words agreed and sure: 25r 37 and 20 of 39; 26r 25 and 17 of 31; 28v 13 and 4 of 19; 56r-57r 37 and 14 of 45; 63r 10 and 6 of 11; 70v 20 and 7 of 27. No sentence containing a run builds with only scattered holes; two clauses read (26r 'Vorrei che V.S. ... mi mandasse ... relatione del'; 57r 'che V.S. haveva scritto per ... viaggio a Dusseldorf'). The six entries stay decoded, not read. Key and cipher words unchanged. Lower 45% of f. 56v fetched once from Penn at full size. No person has checked.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: System B key rebuilt from the Codex 534 interlines and tested on a held-out letter; Codex 533 transcribed twice and its 116 disagreements checked on the image (112 settled); first reading of Cosimo's cipher runs and of the bare 1694 passages. Reading with a key rebuilt from a period decipherment, not an independent solution. Checked by a second AI agent of ours (1r-1v), not by a person.
Anton Francesco Montauti or his secretary: the letter-by-letter interlinear decipherments in Penn Oversize Ms. Codex 534 (ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), the source of every key pair.

texts.label: L01, Codex 533 ff. 1r-1v, undated (after June 1691; breaks off, no date line)
texts.summary: Cosimo tells Montauti that the Elector Palatine has let him know of a report, written to the Elector, that Cosimo's daughter (Anna Maria Luisa, Electress Palatine) had written asking permission to return home and separate from her husband; he says such talk shames and offends his and her reputation, speaks of 'such calumnies', and asks Montauti to act, if need be by going to Düsseldorf. A report at second or third hand that Cosimo treats as calumny; no explicit denial among the words read; the writer to the Elector is unread; undated.
texts.note: Sure words only (README Conventions): 9 of 16 cipher words (56.3%), word by word in readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Not sure: Palatino, ritornare, qua and marito rest on the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q; permission[e] on ww = o and a letter not written; l'El[e]ttor[e] and figl[i]a on a letter supplied or replaced by sense. With the context-only values 13 of 16. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 11 of 16, admitting the two words with a supplied letter. Our earlier figure was 1.0: all 85 cipher groups read as words (two single-letter slips; letters on context-only values and emended digits marked in readings/letter_1r1v.md). The clear text has gaps and needs a palaeographer.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #665 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Cipher runs in the contributor's transcription of the clear text: the letter builds sentences (the Elector Palatine reports that the daughter had written for permission to return and to separate from her husband; Cosimo calls it calumny and asks Montauti to act), with the clear text full of doubt marks. The six runs of f. 1r (69 groups) were compared sign by sign with Penn's IIIF image on 15 Nov 2026: all agree at 1900 px, one 6/0 place in run c not safe at that size. A decoder written here from key/key_v3.json gives the same letters. By sure words 9 of 16, as the contributor now records. The clear text between the runs was not reviewed and needs a palaeographer. Recorded by the reviewer, not by the author; replaces the author's preliminary grade (B, 14 Nov 2026). A model's reading: no person has checked it.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's 35 runs only (Codex 533), counted by words (README Conventions): 30 of 87 words sure (34.5%), every letter from frozen key v3 with no context-only value, no letter supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group; 42 of 87 (48.3%) with the context-only values ww = o and 62 = q. Word list and rule: readings/words_533_strict.tsv. Daniel Bourdeau's review counts 37 of 87 and 51 of 87; the difference is the seven words with a supplied or replaced letter, which his count admits. By groups: 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value. Our earlier figure, about 60% of groups read as Italian, was our estimate between those two. The bare 1694 passages are not included.

gaps.detail: Letters decode in part but form no word; no interline or key covers Cosimo's hand.
No interline gives them; Penn Ms. Coll. 180 Folder 114 (cipher codes 1689, 1694) not seen.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).
